criteria.quote: Hypno makes people sleep, then steals the good dreams.
criteria.revision: Replace the first line with: "Hypno doesn't just put humans to sleep—when it's very hungry, it feasts on their dreams, and anyone having a good one gets carried away."

criteria.quote: When hunger hits, it puts humans it meets to sleep.
criteria.revision: Use the research's sharper condition and action: "When it is very hungry, Hypno puts humans it meets to sleep, then feasts on their dreams."

criteria.quote: Why does Hypno carry away only people having good dreams?
criteria.revision: Change the unanswerable why-question to: "What happens after Hypno puts someone to sleep—and why is a good dream the dangerous one?" Let the final scene answer the first part with the documented dream-feasting and carrying away.

criteria.quote: Its steady pendulum makes anyone nearby drowsy before dreams begin.
criteria.revision: Replace this unsupported sequence with the stronger documented detail: "Seeing its swinging pendulum can induce sleep in three seconds—even in someone who just woke up." Then escalate from immediate sleep to dream-feasting and finally being carried away.

criteria.quote: But anyone having a good dream gets carried away by Hypno.
Hypno makes people sleep, then steals the good dreams.
criteria.revision: Replace the opening scene's repeated sleep-and-dream summary with a distinct behavior: "Avoid eye contact if you come across one—it will try to put you to sleep with its pendulum."

criteria.quote: Hypno's worst hunger turns sleep into a hunt for the dreams it likes best.
criteria.revision: Remove the unsupported "worst hunger" and "likes best" framing. Use: "When Hypno is very hungry, it puts humans to sleep, feasts on their dreams, and carries away anyone having a good one."

criteria.quote: Would you risk sleep, or guard your best dreams?
criteria.revision: Make the closing a genuine evidence-based split: "Is Hypno a danger—or a savior for people who need a good, sound sleep?"
